paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God has already handed you everything. 2 Peter 1:3 says His divine power "has given us everything we need for life and godliness." Not a starter kit. EVERYTHING. And in verse 4, it says you have "escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires," so you're not climbing out of the pit, you're already standing outside it.

Because of that, Peter says, "make every effort." Notice what he's asking. He's not saying work to earn it. He's saying grow in what you've already been given, stacking virtue, knowledge, self-control and the rest, with love at the top (2 Peter 1:5-7). I once tried to stack every topping at the same time, friend, and my apron paid for it. Peter's way is better: one layer at a time, each sitting on the one before.

Why bother? Because these qualities keep you from being "ineffective and unproductive" in knowing Jesus (2 Peter 1:8). And when you forget you've been "cleansed from his past sins," you start seeing like someone nearsighted (2 Peter 1:9). So keep growing, keep remembering, and keep your eyes on the finish, because Peter says a "lavish reception" is waiting in the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ (2 Peter 1:11).
